readingMnemonic: The readings are the kun'yomi reading for 当て and the on'yomi reading for 字 . You've seen 当てる in the past, so you should be able to read this portion as well. Combine the two together and you have yourself a nice reading.

sentences.japanese: 「珈琲」は「コーヒー」の有名な当て字です。
sentences.english: 珈琲 is the well-known phonetic kanji for the word コーヒー (coffee).

sentences.japanese: この本は、当て字を多く使用しているため、少し分かりにくいです。
sentences.english: This book is a bit confusing because it uses a lot of ateji.

sentences.japanese: 「先生、この当て字はどう読むんですか？」と聞くと、先生は少し青い顔になってこう言った。「その読み方は…知らないほうがいいです。今はまだ…ね。」
sentences.english: "Professor, how do you read this ateji?" I asked. She went slightly pale and replied: "You're… better off not knowing that pronunciation. Not yet."

meaningMnemonic: You know how 私 can mean private and how 大 is the first half of 大学 ? Well, combine those together and you have the shortened version of private college or private university .
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. Since 大 has two on'yomi readings, here's a mnemonic to help you remember which one to use: You went to a specific private college just to study dye s ( だい ). You're so into dyes that you decided to go to this extremely expensive private university that specializes in dyes. Good for you!

sentences.english: entrance exam for a private university
to be admitted to a private university, to enroll in a private university
to get into a private university, to enter a private university
to advance to a private university

sentences.japanese: 私大に入学したいと思っています。
sentences.english: I want to enroll in a private college.

sentences.japanese: 私大の学生もバイトしてる子が多いですよ。
sentences.english: Many kids at private universities have a part-time job too.

sentences.japanese: 私大は入学にお金がかかります。
sentences.english: It costs money to enroll in a private university.

meaningMnemonic: You've seen how 鉄 often has to do with railroad tracks, and this word is no exception — a private iron is a private railway . In Japan, 私鉄 is the word for privately operated railway companies that were never part of the national Japan Railways system. Think of the big, non-JR commuter railways like Tokyu and Odakyu in Tokyo, or Hankyu in Kansai.
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

sentences.japanese: 四月に私鉄の会社に入社しました。
sentences.english: I joined a private railway company in April.

sentences.japanese: 東京のこの辺りは、私鉄もJRも通ってて、土地がすごく高いですよ。
sentences.english: The property values around this area of ​​Tokyo are very high because both a private railway and a JR line are running through here.

sentences.japanese: 東京には、JRや東京メトロなどの他にも、たくさんの私鉄が走っています。
sentences.english: In Tokyo, besides JR and Tokyo Metro, there are also many private railway lines.

meaningMnemonic: Picture the part of your body that makes up your neck . Are you picturing it? That's a building block that makes up your body. A really important one. If you didn't have that neck, you wouldn't look like a person at all. Sound familiar? It should! Because that part of your neck is a radical ! Just like part of your neck is a building block of your body, the radical is a building block of kanji. Get it? I sure hope so!
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You haven't learned this reading for 首 yet, so here's a mnemonic to help you: When you need a radical to make a new kanji, you just press a button and the radical comes tumbling down the radical chu te ( しゅ ). There's definitely no rhyme or reason to radical picking, it's just whatever pops out of the ol' chute.

sentences.japanese: この字の部首は何ですか？
sentences.english: What is the radical of this character?

sentences.japanese: 部首の名前はたくさんあります。

sentences.english: The radical for the kanji for "cut" is "sword."

meaningMnemonic: A line that runs on a road is a railroad track . First you have to get into your mind that the "line" in question is a railway line. Then, what railway line runs on a road and what kind of road is it? It's a railroad track .
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

sentences.english: to run on the railroad tracks
to walk along the railroad track
on the other side of the railroad tracks

sentences.japanese: 線路には、何があっても入らないで下さい。
sentences.english: Never go on the railroad tracks, no matter what.

sentences.japanese: 家の前に線路があるので、電車の音が大きいです。
sentences.english: There is a train track in front of the house, so the noise from the train is loud.

sentences.japanese: 兄は必ず線路が見えるよう、電車の後ろの車両に乗ります。
sentences.english: My older brother always gets on the last car of the train so that he can see the train tracks.

meaningMnemonic: The most nearby is something that happened close to now. It happened recently .
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

sentences.japanese: 最近まで知らなかった
最近は出社しないで家でリモートワークをしています。
sentences.english: Lately, I don't go to work and work remotely from home.

sentences.japanese: 最近、私は自立の仕方を本気で考えています。
sentences.english: Recently, I am seriously thinking about a way to become independent.

sentences.japanese: テレビを持ってないので、最近の有名人や人気の曲を全く知りません。
sentences.english: I don't have a TV, so I don't know any recent celebrities or popular songs.

meaningMnemonic: You've seen that 研究 is "research" from previous vocab, and you might remember 所 can mean "facility." So this word means research institute or, of course, research facility .
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well. It will also help if you know the reading of 研究 already. Also note that 所 is normal in first reading, but gets rendaku'd in the second reading, meaning しょ becomes じょ . Both readings are valid and they don't affect the meaning, so it just comes down to personal preference!

sentences.japanese: ここは、全国でも有名な研究所です。
sentences.english: This research institute is famous throughout the country.

sentences.japanese: このシャンプーは、アメリカの研究所で、生まれました。
sentences.english: This shampoo was created at a research institute in the United States.

sentences.japanese: 平日は、日本語研究所で平安時代の文学の研究をしています。
sentences.english: On weekdays, I research literature from the Heian era at the laboratory of Japanese language.

meaningMnemonic: You revolve X number of times . Really, the times isn't so important, but the revolving is. That's why this word is revolve or rotate .
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well. P.S. Ever heard of " 回転ずし ?" That's the kind of sushi that's on conveyor belts, rotating around and around, bringing you delicious plates of things.

sentences.english: sushi served on a conveyor belt

sentences.japanese: 車は、走る時にタイヤが回転します。
sentences.english: The tires revolve when the car runs.

sentences.japanese: これは、ペットのハムスターが回し車を回転させている音です。
sentences.english: This is the sound of a pet hamster spinning their wheel.

sentences.japanese: 先日、回転ずし屋に出かけました。
sentences.english: The other day, I went to a revolving sushi restaurant.

meaningMnemonic: This is just the noun version of the kanji 酒 - it has an お there to be nice. This word can mean both alcohol (like the parent kanji) or sake (the main kind of Japanese alcohol, at least back in the kanji days).
readingMnemonic: The reading is kun'yomi, which isn't what you learned with the kanji. But, it should be pretty easy. You know what Japanese alcohol is called already, right? It's さけ , simple as that. So long as you've heard of sake you should be A-Okay with this reading.

sentences.english: to like to drink alcohol every now and then, to drink just to be sociable

sentences.japanese: このドリンクはお酒が入ってますか？
日本で、お酒を飲めるのは二十才以上の大人だけです。
sentences.english: In Japan, only adults over twenty years old can drink.

sentences.japanese: お酒に弱いので、お茶をいただきます。
sentences.english: I don't have much alcohol tolerance, so I will have tea.

meaningMnemonic: This is the equivalent of the English word service . By extension, it's often used to mean a freebie . Though it's generally used as a standard noun, it can also be a verbal noun used with する . In this case, it means giving a freebie .

sentences.japanese: あのレストランのサービス、ビミョーじゃない？
sentences.english: The service at that restaurant isn't great, is it?

sentences.japanese: えー、ただのリップサービスじゃない？
sentences.english: Eh, it's just lip service, isn't it?

sentences.japanese: クリームパン買ったら、パンの耳、サービスしてくれた。
sentences.english: When I bought cream buns, they gave me bread crusts for free.

meaningMnemonic: Taking the nearby road will get you to your destination more quickly (because it's more close by!). This is a shortcut , aka the short way .
readingMnemonic: The reading is a bit weird in this one. It uses the kun'yomi reading for both kanji, even though it looks just like it should be all on'yomi reading. It's like you're taking a shortcut with your kanji readings and doing the native Japanese readings (kun'yomi) instead of the more intellectual Chinese ones (on'yomi). Luckily, you've hopefully seen both of these kanji as vocab already. You have ちか for 近 (short for 近い ) and you have 道 ( みち ), just like the word "street" you learned before. Combine these together and you have the reading for this word. Perhaps it's like this because you're combining a couple concepts together into one word, at least when it comes to "short + way."

sentences.english: to tell someone about a shortcut

sentences.japanese: この道を右に曲がった方が、近道ですよ。
sentences.english: There's a shortcut if you turn down this road to the right.

sentences.japanese: 全ての近道が、安全な道という事じゃない。
sentences.english: Not all shortcuts are safe roads.

sentences.japanese: 近道をすると、花見の場所にすぐに行けますよ。
sentences.english: If you take a shortcut, you can go to the cherry blossom viewing venue quickly.

meaningMnemonic: When your energy is that of sick ness, you are probably sick .
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

sentences.english: to not lose to illness, to not let illness get the better of oneself
to spread a disease to someone

sentences.japanese: ドライアイは目の病気です。
sentences.english: Dry eye is an eye disease.

sentences.japanese: 昨日、クラスメイトが病気で学校を休みました。
sentences.english: Yesterday, my classmates didn't come to school due to an illness.

sentences.japanese: 病気の時は、早くベッドに行って、よく休むことが重要です。
sentences.english: When you are sick, it is important to go to bed early and have a good rest.

meaningMnemonic: A person who is sick is a sick person . They are also a patient , at least we can hope they are, for their sake.
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. Since 人 has two on'yomi readings, here's a mnemonic to help you remember which one to use: Every sick person enjoys playing on their Nin tendo ( にん ). You have the nastiest flu, but you've still got your Nintendo, so everything is fine.

sentences.english: to look at a sick person

sentences.japanese: 病人や、ケガ人はいますか？
病人には早くよくなってほしいですが、やっぱり近づかないでほしいです。
sentences.english: I want the patients to feel better soon, but still I don't want them to come near me.

sentences.japanese: お母さん、病人にそんな重い物持たさないでよ！
sentences.english: Mom, don't let a sick person carry such heavy stuff!

sentences.japanese: うちの姉は病人に対してだけ天使のように親切にする事ができます。
sentences.english: My sister can be kind of like an angel to sick people.

meaningMnemonic: The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. Please note that this word refers to "the side of something." Not "the left side," for example. That would be 左側 .
readingMnemonic: The reading for this vocab is the same as the one you learned with the kanji, lucky you!

sentences.english: to be next to someone, to be next to something
to be next to someone, to be next to something

sentences.japanese: ベランダのプランターの横に毛虫がいた。
sentences.english: There was a caterpillar next to the planter on the balcony.

sentences.japanese: 家の横に木で出来たフェンスが立っています。
sentences.english: There's a fence made of wood standing next to the house.

sentences.japanese: 横でボーっと見てないで、あんたも助けてよ！
sentences.english: Don't just stand to the side watching — help out!

meaningMnemonic: Remember how 手 can sometimes mean “doer”? What do you think a song doer is? A singer , of course
readingMnemonic: The readings are on'yomi readings. You've learned them both already (you learned 手 's on'yomi reading with word 投手 ), so you should be able to read this like a singer sings with a bunch of cashew s かしゅ in their mouth. FAST AND LOUD!

sentences.japanese: 会社をやめて、今すぐ歌手になりたい。
sentences.english: I want to quit the company and become a singer right now.

sentences.japanese: レストランには日本人のピアニストと歌手がいました。
sentences.english: There was a Japanese pianist and singer at the restaurant.

sentences.japanese: シンディ・ローパーはニューヨーク出身の有名な歌手です。
sentences.english: Cindy Lauper is a famous singer from New York.

meaningMnemonic: You sit down to solve an issue and firmly decide on your course of action. This process is called solving , and it leads to a solution and settlement . 解決 is about finding a resolution or bringing a matter to a close. It can be used either for small-scale personal problems or for large-scale problems like social and political issues.
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

sentences.english: to get to work on a solution

sentences.japanese: コウイチはお金で何でも解決できると思っている。
sentences.english: Koichi thinks he can solve any problem with money.

sentences.japanese: これですべてが解決したと思うのはまだ早いよ。
sentences.english: It's still too early to think that everything has been solved.

sentences.japanese: 「ただそこに立っているだけでは、何の解決にもなりませんよ」と、フグはきっぱりと言った。
sentences.english: "Just standing there won't solve anything," said Fugu bluntly.

sentences.japanese: どう解決したらいいのか、全く分からないんだよね。
sentences.english: I have absolutely no idea how to solve this.

meaningMnemonic: One of the kanji's meanings is song and this word means exactly that: a song .
readingMnemonic: Since this word is made up of a single kanji, it should use the kun'yomi reading. When learning the kanji, you didn't learn that reading, so here's a mnemonic to help you with this word: Think about a song... but not just any song... think about the utter ( うた ) song, and make it up right now and sing it out loud. What does the utter song sound like? Why do you love utterances so much that you made a song about them?

sentences.english: to sing to oneself, to hum a tune

sentences.japanese: これって、日本の歌ですよね？
sentences.english: This is a Japanese song, isn't it?

sentences.japanese: 今日ショッピングモールでかかってた歌の名前、知ってますか？
sentences.english: Do you know the name of the song that was playing at the shopping mall today?

sentences.japanese: 君のために作った歌だよ。
sentences.english: It's a song I made for you.

meaningMnemonic: The South East is the Southeast .
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings for both kanji. You've seen those readings before in 南米 and 東京 , for example, so you should be good to go here!

sentences.english: to be located to the southeast
to head southeast, to face southeast

sentences.japanese: 車は、南東の方に行った。
sentences.english: The car went in a southeast direction.

sentences.japanese: 会社のビルは南東を向いています。
sentences.english: The office building is facing southeast.

sentences.japanese: 南東は、よく日が当たります。
sentences.english: The southeast gets good sun light.

meaningMnemonic: You can probably figure out that スペイン is "Spain" just by reading it. Add the kanji language on there and you have the Spanish language (or just Spanish ), if you'd like.
readingMnemonic: The reading for the kanji portion is just the reading you learned with the kanji. Since it's attached to something, it's like a jukugo word.

sentences.japanese: スペイン語のアクセント
スペイン語のテキスト
友人にスペイン語を教えてあげました。
スペイン語の発音は、日本語の発音と大体同じらしいですよ。
sentences.english: Apparently, the pronunciation of Spanish is about the same as Japanese pronunciation.

sentences.japanese: ニンニクはスペイン語で「ajo」っていうんだけど、「アホ」って発音されるんだよ。「アホ」は日本語で「stupid」って意味だよ。
sentences.english: Garlic in Spanish is "ajo," which is pronounced "aho." "Aho" means "stupid" in Japanese.

meaningMnemonic: Your fast ness degree is your speed . You use 速度 to talk about a specific speed of something like a car or a train. If you want to talk about speed more casually, you can just say スピード or 速さ .
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

sentences.japanese: インターネットの速度がおそすぎてイライラしています。
sentences.english: These internet speeds are too slow and it’s pissing me off.

sentences.japanese: もう少し速度を下げて走行してください。
sentences.english: Lower the speed a little more, please.

sentences.japanese: 姉は朝ごはんの食パンを口に入れたまま、すごい速度で学校に走っていきました。
sentences.english: My older sister ran to school at such an incredible speed, with bread in her mouth.

meaningMnemonic: 立つ means "to stand," and 飲む means "to drink," right? Well, when you do both at the same time, you're standing and drinking or drinking while standing . It also refers to casual standing bar s where there are no seats — customers stand while having drinks and light snacks.
readingMnemonic: The readings are from the words 立つ and 飲む put together.

sentences.japanese: この立ち飲み屋は、生ビールが安くて、おつまみもおいしいですよ。
sentences.english: This standing bar has cheap draft beers and delicious drinking snacks.

sentences.japanese: 一時間後の電車に乗るので、立ち飲みで平気ですよ。
sentences.english: Drinking while standing works for me as I'll be taking a train an hour later.

sentences.japanese: 先日、立ち飲みバーでウイスキーをのんでいたら色々な人と出会いました。
sentences.english: The other day, I met various people while drinking whiskey at a standing bar.

meaningMnemonic: The open of the start is the start or beginning . Note that 開始 is slightly more formal than 始める .
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

sentences.japanese: イベントの開始時間は何時ですか？
sentences.english: What time does the event start?

sentences.japanese: 明日から新しいプロジェクトが開始します。
sentences.english: A new project will start tomorrow.

sentences.japanese: ミーティングの開始がおくれるって、社長にはもう言った？
sentences.english: Did you tell the president that the start time for the meeting will be delayed?

meaningMnemonic: The kanji version of 話 means talk . This word also means talk , but it means a few other things as well. This can refer to a speech or story as well. Basically anything that involves a talking session. So, before you go, I hope you stay awhile and listen to my 話 .
readingMnemonic: Hey, tell that story about the time you met the 花 -shee p ( はなし ). You know — the sheep that had 花 s growing out of it instead of wool. No one else here has ever met a 花 -sheep, so I bet they'd all love to hear your story.

sentences.english: to become a certain topic in conversation
other people's talk, talk about other people
a topic of conversation comes up
to have something to say to someone
to return to a prior point of discussion
to listen to what someone has to say

sentences.japanese: 同じ話を何回されても、よく分かりません。
sentences.english: No matter how many times you tell me the same story, I still don't understand.

sentences.japanese: また日本のトイレの話ですか？
sentences.english: A talk about Japanese toilets again?

sentences.japanese: 少しだけでいいので、話を聞いてもらえないですか？
sentences.english: Could you listen to me for just a little bit?

meaningMnemonic: A straight line is a straight line . You know, the shortest distance between two points and all that.
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

sentences.english: to join with a straight line
to connect with a straight line
to be connected with a straight line
to run along a straight line

sentences.japanese: 紙に直線を引いてください。
sentences.english: Please draw a straight line on the paper.

sentences.japanese: この図形は三本の直線でできています。
sentences.english: This shape is made of three straight lines.

sentences.japanese: ふと前を見ると、白い石が直線上にならんでいました。
sentences.english: When I glanced ahead, there was a straight row of white stones.

meaningMnemonic: A man made of iron is a strong man ... aka a huge badass . Have you seen "Iron Chef?" The Japanese translation is 料理の鉄人 , which means "Chef Iron Man" aka "Chef Badass," at least in my book.
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. Since 人 has two on'yomi readings, here's a mnemonic to help you remember which one to use: Check out the strong man wearing nothing but jean s ( じん ). He looks like a badass in his jeans, flexing his pecs. Very impressive, but also slightly terrifying.

sentences.japanese: うちの社長はトライアスロンの後に出社するような鉄人です。
sentences.english: Our president is a strong man who comes to work after a triathlon.

sentences.japanese: この有名女子プロレスラーは鉄人のように強いです。
sentences.english: This famous female professional wrestler is strong like a badass.

sentences.japanese: あの男の人は、かつては「鉄人シェフ」とよばれたフレンチシェフです。
sentences.english: That man is a French chef, who was once also called the "Iron Chef."

sentences.japanese: スーパーで赤ちゃんに「いないいないばぁ」をしている鉄人を見てしまった。
sentences.english: I saw a tough guy playing peak-a-boo with a baby in a grocery store.

meaningMnemonic: The main thing you talk about in your language becomes the subject of the sentence.
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

sentences.japanese: この文の主語は何ですか？
sentences.english: What is the subject of this sentence?

sentences.japanese: 先週の日本語のクラスで、日本語の主語について学びました。
sentences.english: In Japanese class last week, I learned about subjects in Japanese.

sentences.japanese: 日本語では、いちいち主語を言わなくても相手に分かってもらえる事が多いんですよね。
sentences.english: In Japanese, even if you don't say the subject every time, the listener would often get it.

meaningMnemonic: Remember how 引く means "to pull" and "to withdraw"? Well, if you calculate by pulling or withdrawing one number out of another, you're doing subtraction . Kinda like how your bank balance gets lower every time you subtract (withdraw) money from it, you know?
readingMnemonic: This is the kun'yomi reading for 引 and the on'yomi for 算 . And the さん reading is rendaku'd into ざん . This is the same for all the math-ish words (addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division), so try to remember that, because you'll see it again!

sentences.japanese: もちろん、わたしは引き算ができます！
sentences.english: Of course I can do subtraction!

sentences.japanese: 引き算は、たとえば「六から二を引いて、答えが四」ということです。
sentences.english: A subtraction, for example, is "subtracting two from six equals four."

sentences.japanese: 小学校三年生レベルの引き算なのに、答えがどうしても分からない。
sentences.english: Although it is a elementary school third grade level subtraction problem, I still can't figure out the answer.

meaningMnemonic: The ground below iron is iron under the ground. It isn't a deposit of iron, though. It's man-made. And what's made of iron? Trains. In this case, because it's underground, it's a subway . Depending on where you live, you might call it the Underground , the Tube , or the Metro
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

sentences.japanese: 私は地下鉄に乗って大学へ行っていました。
sentences.english: I used to ride the subway to college.

sentences.japanese: 地下鉄の出口は色々な所にあります。
sentences.english: There are subway exits in various places.

sentences.japanese: ニューヨークの地下鉄には本当に色々な人が乗ってますね。

meaningMnemonic: The most tall isn't literally the most tall. When you think of something high above the rest, you think of something that is the best .
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

sentences.english: the best something in one's life

sentences.english: Shaved ice is best to eat in summer.

sentences.japanese: 仕事が終わってからのビールは、やっぱり最高だな。
sentences.english: Having a beer after work is the best.

sentences.japanese: この名曲は何十年も人気があり、J-POPヒストリー上最高の音楽として知られています。
sentences.english: This masterpiece has been popular for decades and is known as the best music in J-pop history.

meaningMnemonic: You've seen 一番 (number one), but what is this eye on the end? Like in the word 〜丁目 , the 目 here marks a position in a sequence. So, add this to "number one" and you have the first thing or simply the first . Just imagine your collection of eyeballs you have at home. (You have a collection of eyeballs, right?) You have them lined up in a display case and you're explaining the first one to your friend. It's not first because it's the best or anything — you love all your eyeballs equally, after all — but it does happen to come first in sequence in your display right now.
readingMnemonic: The reading for this word is just the vocab word 一番 plus the word 目 . If you know both of those readings you'll be able to read this one as well.

sentences.japanese: 右に曲がって一番目の部屋に入ってください。
sentences.english: Please turn right and enter the first room.

sentences.japanese: その朝、一番目に家を出たのは兄でした。
sentences.english: On that morning, my older brother was the first to leave the house.

sentences.japanese: 東京大学に入学できる事を一番目に知らせたかった人は、受験中ずっと支えてくれた父でした。
sentences.english: The first person who I wanted to inform that I would be admitted to the University of Tokyo was my father, who supported me throughout my entrance exams.

meaningMnemonic: This is the adverb version of the kanji, so it has the same meaning, basically. You can say this is the most or just most . You can also use it as extremely .
readingMnemonic: The reading for this is a reading you didn't learn with the kanji (the kun'yomi reading). To learn it, let's look at a mnemonic. Think of the most ridiculous motto ( もっと ) you've ever heard. Now imagine a motto that's even more ridiculous. Here are some actual totally real mottos that are the most ridiculous: "What Can Brown Do for You?" "It's Not for Women" "If It Doesn't Get All Over the Place, It Doesn't Belong in Your Face" and of course, "Why Not Enjoy the Go?"

sentences.japanese: ふじ山は日本で最も高い山です。
sentences.english: Mt. Fuji is the highest mountain in Japan.

sentences.japanese: アメフトでは、最もスコアが高いチームが勝者となります。
sentences.english: In American football, the team with the highest score is the winner.

sentences.japanese: 人生で最も大切な物は何ですか？お金ですか？それとも自由ですか？
sentences.english: What is the most important thing in life? Is it money? Or is it freedom?

meaningMnemonic: Now morning is just another way of saying this morning . It's the closest morning to right now!
readingMnemonic: This reading is an exception. Let's use this mnemonic to remember it: This morning you want a quesa dilla ( けさ ) for breakfast. You can't wait until tomorrow morning, you NEED it this morning! Imagine eating a delicious quesadilla first thing this morning. Mmm!

sentences.english: to wake up early this morning

sentences.japanese: 今朝になってから「あ！テスト今日じゃん！」って思い出したんです。
sentences.english: I remembered this morning, "Oh! The exam is today!"

sentences.japanese: 今朝は思ったより冬らしい天気だったので、コートで会社に行きました。
sentences.english: This morning, it was more winter-ish weather than I expected, so I went to work in my coat.

sentences.japanese: 今朝は早く起きて、お父さんと一緒に手作りの朝食を作った。
sentences.english: I got up early this morning and made a handmade breakfast with my dad.

meaningMnemonic: This word consists of kanji with hiragana attached. Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means advance so the verb vocab version means to advance . 進む is an intransitive verb, meaning it describes something or someone moving ( む ) forward. It can be used for physical movement, like a person walking forward or a clock running fast, or for abstract progress, like in someone's work or studies.
readingMnemonic: Since this word consists of a kanji with hiragana attached, you can bet that it will use the kun'yomi reading. You didn't learn that reading with this kanji, so here's a mnemonic to help you: In order to advance , you must sue Sue ( すす ) for her misdeeds against you. Imagine her standing in your way, literally. She keeps saying, "You'll have to sue me if you want to move forward !" So you do — you sue Sue. That way, you can finally move on with your life.

sentences.japanese: もう少し前に進んで下さい。
sentences.english: Please move a little more forward.

sentences.japanese: プロジェクトは進んでますか？
アクセルをふんでるのに、なぜか車が進みません。
sentences.english: The car does not go forward for some reason, even though I'm stepping on the gas pedal.

meaningMnemonic: タバコ is the Japanese version of the Portuguese word "tabaco." You probably won’t be shocked to learn that タバコ means tobacco or cigarette in English! Watch out for the first syllable, which is タ and not ト . タバコ can also be written in hiragana, and even in kanji, but katakana is the most common by far.

sentences.japanese: あ、タバコのにおいがする。
sentences.english: Oh, I can smell cigarette smoke.

sentences.japanese: タバコが中々やめられないんだ。
sentences.english: I've been struggling to quit smoking.

sentences.japanese: 歩きタバコはよくないよ。
sentences.english: It's not good to smoke while walking.

meaningMnemonic: This word consists of kanji with hiragana attached. Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means begin or start , and the verb version is to begin , to begin something , to start , or to start something . This is a transitive verb. That means it takes a direct object. You start something. Like studying! You should have started studying earlier though, huh?
readingMnemonic: Since this word has okurigana (hiragana attached to the kanji) you know that it's probably going to be the kun'yomi reading, which you didn't learn with the kanji. Here's a mnemonic to help you: Right now it's time to begin Haj ( はじ ). (Haj is the fifth pillar of Islam, and is a pilgrimage to Mecca during the month of Dhu al-Hijja). You need to start Haj right now!

sentences.japanese: すきなところから始める
sentences.english: to start from where one likes

sentences.japanese: できることから始める
sentences.english: to start with what one can do

sentences.japanese: 去年、名古屋での新しい生活を始めました。
sentences.english: Last year, I started a new life in Nagoya.

sentences.japanese: 私は、まだワニカニを始めたばかりです。
スペイン語を学びたいけど、何から始めるのがいいのか、分かりません。
sentences.english: I want to learn Spanish, but I don't know where to start.

meaningMnemonic: You know that 助ける means "to help." This word, 助かる , is related, but it's a bit different. It means to be helped or to be saved . It's intransitive, so it doesn't take a direct object. Imagine shouting "I'm saved!" No direct object, right? Verbs ending in okurigana that rhyme with ある tend to be intransitive like this. You can remember this because if something is ある , it's just there, existing, not acting on anything else. That's why verbs that sound like it are often intransitive too!
readingMnemonic: The reading is the same as 助ける , so hopefully you know that word and can apply that knowledge over here.

sentences.english: to find it helpful to have the day off
will be saved thanks to someone
I'm sure they'll be fine. It's okay.

sentences.japanese: 家を出たら、目の前にタクシーがいて、助かった。
sentences.english: When I left the house, there was a taxi right in front of my eyes and I was saved.

sentences.japanese: 今回の試験については、どんな答えを聞かれるか、先生が前もって教えてくれたので、とても助かった。
sentences.english: The teacher told us in advance what kind of answers we will be asked for on this test, which was very helpful.

meaningMnemonic: This word consists of kanji with hiragana attached. Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji 点 means point , but this verb actually means to be lit or to be ignited . Think of it this way, when a flashlight turns on, it points a beam, of light. You already learned 点ける , which is for when you turn something on. 点く , on the other hand, is an intransitive verb. That means it happens by itself. Like, "Oh look! The lights came on! That's cool ( く )!"
readingMnemonic: You already learned this reading when you learned 点ける but here's a mnemonic just in case: Every time you count to two ( つ ) a light comes on. How cool that it does it all by itself!!

sentences.japanese: 人が来ると、セキュリティのためのライトが点くんです。
sentences.english: When people come, the security lights turn on.

sentences.japanese: やっとキャンドルに火が点いて、テーブルの上は明るくなりました。
sentences.english: Finally the candles were lit, and the tabletop got brighter.

sentences.japanese: 「アレクサ、電気を点けて」と言うと、家の全ての電気が点きます。
sentences.english: When I say "Alexa, turn the lights on," all the lights in the house turn on.

meaningMnemonic: This word consists of kanji with hiragana attached. Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means reflect . The verb vocab version means to be reflected . You're not doing the reflecting directly. You can remember this by thinking how rude ( る ) it is that someone's reflecting your image using a mirror for everyone outside the dressing room to see.
readingMnemonic: Since this word consists of a kanji with hiragana attached, you can bet that it will use the kun'yomi reading. You didn't learn that reading with this kanji, so here's a mnemonic to help you: Your reflection is getting reflected onto the mirror. You don't like it, it doesn't look like you. Impostor reflection! You take a hammer and you 打つ ( うつ ) it as hard as you can, glass flying everywhere. Then some dubstep starts playing from the broken mirror: うつ うつうつうつ . You might recall that this reading is the same as 写 る and might wonder if they're related. They are! They both talk about the image of something showing up somewhere else, and use different kanji to distinguish where. In 写る 's case, that would typically be in photographs, and for 映る , it's in reflections or projections (which includes the contents of screens, like those of TVs or computers).

sentences.english: to see, to be reflected in someone's eyes
to be reflected in the mirror

sentences.japanese: スクリーンにパスワードが映っていますよ。
sentences.english: The password is being projected on the screen.

sentences.japanese: テレビに映ると太って見えるって本当ですか？
sentences.english: Is it true that you look fatter on TV?

sentences.japanese: ちゃんとスクリーンに映るかな。
sentences.english: I wonder if it will properly appear on the screen.

sentences.japanese: 今、テレビにお父さん映らなかった？
sentences.english: Didn't Dad appear on TV just now?

sentences.japanese: テレビ電話をしていると、犬の顔がひょっこり映ってほっこりした。
sentences.english: During the video call, the dog's face unexpectedly appeared and it was heartwarming.

sentences.japanese: その夜、君と二人で見た、あの水に映る美しい月が忘れられません。
sentences.english: I can't forget the beautiful moon reflected in the water that we saw together that night.

meaningMnemonic: You've seen the word 化ける (to transform) before, and here's a related word: 化かす . This means to bewitch , to trick , or to deceive . Why? In Japanese folklore, foxes, spirits and other yokai often transform in order to bewitch, trick, or deceive humans. To 化かす them, in other words. This verb is transitive, so it needs a direct object — you bewitch, trick, or deceive someone. You know this because when a fox wants to bewitch someone, they have to cuss ( かす ). They say a magic cuss word that lets them change forms and fool people. Those tricksy foxes…
readingMnemonic: The reading is the same as 化ける , so make sure you know that word and you'll be able to learn this word's reading as well.

sentences.english: to bewitch people, to deceive people
to bewitch villagers, to deceive villagers
to bewitch a person, to deceive a person

sentences.japanese: 日本では、タヌキは人間を化かす生物だと言われている。
sentences.english: In Japan, raccoons are said to be creatures that bewitch humans.

sentences.japanese: このキツネは人を化かす天才だ。
sentences.english: This fox is a genius at enchanting people.

sentences.japanese: 「先日は来れなくて、すみませんでした。キツネに化かされちまってねえ。」「心配しないでください。それはどうしようもない事ですから。」
sentences.english: "I’m sorry I couldn't make it the other day. I was bewitched by a fox." "No worries. Things like that can’t be helped."

meaningMnemonic: This word consists of kanji with hiragana attached. Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means carry so the verb version is to carry .
readingMnemonic: Since this word consists of a kanji with hiragana attached, you can bet that it will use the kun'yomi reading. You didn't learn that reading with this kanji, so here's a mnemonic to help you: Imagine you have to carry a har d co re ( はこ ) music fan home after a concert. They spent all night moshing to hardcore sounds, and now they’re too tired to walk. But you? You’re a hardcore friend, so you’re happy to carry them.

sentences.japanese: イベントがスムーズに運ぶ
鳥が木の一部を運ぶのを見ました。
sentences.english: I saw a bird carrying a part of the tree.

sentences.japanese: お茶を、お客さんの部屋に運びました。
sentences.english: I brought tea to the customer's room.

sentences.japanese: えっ、一人で三つのスーツケースを運んだんですか？
sentences.english: What? Did you carry all three suitcases by yourself?

meaningMnemonic: This word consists of kanji with hiragana attached. Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means collect and this verb is transitive, meaning the action is done to something or someone. So this verb means things like to collect something and to gather something .
readingMnemonic: Since this word consists of a kanji with hiragana attached, you can bet that it will use the kun'yomi reading. You didn't learn that reading with this kanji, so here's a mnemonic to help you: You have one of something, but that's not much of a collection. What should you get if you want to collect something ? Ah, two ( あつ )! Two of that thing! Yes, when you have enough to say "Ah, two…" you know you've really begun to collect something. Ah, two Crabigator trading cards! See?

sentences.japanese: 私は古いビー玉を集めるのが、すきです。
全国から美しい花を集めて、手作りのブーケを作りました。
sentences.english: We collected beautiful flowers from all over the country and made handmade bouquets.

sentences.japanese: ユーザーからのフィードバックを集めています。
sentences.english: We are collecting feedback from users.

meaningMnemonic: A 決定 is a "decision." So, when you add する to it you're making it a verb, meaning this word means to decide .
readingMnemonic: The reading is the same as 決定 with する added. Make sure you know 決定 and you'll know this word as well.

sentences.english: the date and time are decided
to decide the date and time

sentences.japanese: コウイチの赤ちゃんの名前が決定したら、すぐにお知らせしますね。
sentences.english: Once they've decided on a name for Koichi's baby, I'll let you know right away.

sentences.japanese: コンテストの勝者を決定しました。
sentences.english: The winner of the contest has been decided.

sentences.japanese: クソワロタwwwこのテレビ番組クソほどおもしろいじゃねーかよ。俺の一番好きな番組に決定したわ。
sentences.english: ROFL! This TV show is hilarious, man. I’ve decided that this is now my new favorite show.

meaningMnemonic: This word consists of kanji with hiragana attached. Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means decide so the verb version is to decide .
readingMnemonic: Since this word consists of a kanji with hiragana attached, you can bet that it will use the kun'yomi reading. You didn't learn that reading with this kanji, so here's a mnemonic to help you: You have to decide . You have two key s ( き ) in front of you. You have to decide on one of them and use it to unlock the door to get away from the monster. Why do monster attacks always come down to keys and doors?

sentences.japanese: 毎日、ネクタイを決めるのに時間がかかります。
sentences.english: It takes time to decide which tie to wear every day.

sentences.japanese: 私立大学に入学することに決めました。
sentences.english: I decided to enroll in a private university.

sentences.japanese: 今日の夜、コウイチと行くレストランは、もう決めましたか？
sentences.english: Have you decided on the restaurant you'll go to with Koichi tonight?

meaningMnemonic: This word consists of kanji with hiragana attached. Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means distribute so the verb vocab version is to distribute .
readingMnemonic: Since this word consists of a kanji with hiragana attached, you can bet that it will use the kun'yomi reading. You didn't learn that reading with this kanji, so here's a mnemonic to help you: You’re going to distribute flyers about your favorite country: Cuba ( くば ). You’re the biggest Cubaboo there has ever been, so you’ll gladly stand out in the street distributing flyers about Cuba all day long… right?

sentences.english: to keep a watchful eye on someone

sentences.japanese: 先生が試験の紙を配る。
sentences.english: The teacher distributes the paper for the exam.

sentences.japanese: 日本の女子学生たちは、バレンタインデーに学校で手作りのチョコレートを配るんです。
sentences.english: Female students in Japan pass out handmade chocolates at school on Valentine's Day.

sentences.japanese: 新聞を配るバイトって、ランニングしながらでも出来ますか？
sentences.english: Can I do a part-time job to distribute newspapers while running?

sentences.japanese: このパーティー、本気でつまんない。道でティシュでも配ってる方がマシだよ。
sentences.english: This party blows. Even passing out pocket tissues on the street would be better.

meaningMnemonic: This word consists of kanji with hiragana attached. Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means drink so the vocab verb version is to drink .
readingMnemonic: The reading is the same as the one you learned with the kanji. Go have a drink in the great Allicrab's name!

sentences.english: My mother drinks tea every day.

sentences.japanese: 兄は一気にウイスキーを飲んで顔が赤くなった。
sentences.english: My brother drank some whiskey and his face turned red all at once.

sentences.japanese: この水道水は飲めますか？
sentences.english: Can you drink this tap water?

sentences.japanese: 何をお飲みになりますか？ ジン、ウォッカ、ビール、ワイン、日本酒、それともチューハイ？ 何でも言ってくださいね。お酒なら何でもありますから。
sentences.english: What would you like to drink? Gin, vodka, beer, wine, sake, or chuhai? You name it, we’ve got anything that has alcohol in it.

meaningMnemonic: A thing that carries rotation s (think wheels!) is most kinds of vehicles. So, it's kind of like saying you're "doing vehicles" here... but that doesn't make sense. What do you do to vehicles though? You drive them. That's why this word means to drive .
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word with the on'yomi readings you learned, plus する attached at the end to turn it into a verb. As long as you know the readings of your kanji, you'll know how to read this as well.

sentences.japanese: 父は毎日、会社と家の間を車かバイクで運転する。
sentences.english: My father drives his car or motorcycle every day between his company and home.

sentences.japanese: 船を運転するライセンスは持ってますか？
sentences.english: Do you have a license to steer a ship?

meaningMnemonic: This word consists of kanji with hiragana attached. Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means end , so this verb means to end or to be over . Verbs ending in okurigana that rhyme with ある tend to be intransitive, and 終わる is usually intransitive too. But sometimes it can be transitive and take a direct object. Kind of like "to end" in English — you can say the class ends (intransitive) or a teacher ends their class (transitive).
readingMnemonic: Since this word consists of a kanji with hiragana attached, you can bet that it will use the kun'yomi reading. You didn't learn that reading with this kanji, so here's a mnemonic to help you: This situation has to end . You're the ower ( おわ ) of a lot of money. For this to end, you need to pay back all that money. Try to think of ways to stop being an ower so this stressful situation can end!

sentences.english: work ends, a job is finished

sentences.japanese: 夏休みが終わる前に、海に行きたいです。
sentences.english: I want to go to the ocean before the summer vacation is over.

sentences.japanese: 今日のクラスは全て終わりました。
スタジオの前の道路の工事が中々終わらないので、ポッドキャストのレコーディングに集中できません。
sentences.english: The construction of the road in front of the studio is taking time to be completed, so I can't concentrate on recording podcasts.

meaningMnemonic: You've hopefully seen the word 楽しい , which means "fun." This is basically the verb version (ends in an う sound, right?) of that. That means this is to enjoy something , or just to have fun .
readingMnemonic: The reading is the same as the word 楽しい , so be sure to know that word and you'll be able to apply it over here.

sentences.english: to enjoy as parents and children

sentences.english: Summer is the season to eat shaved ice and enjoy fireworks.

sentences.japanese: 今週末は、友人たちと川でバーベキューを楽しむ予定だ。
sentences.english: This weekend, I'm planning to enjoy a barbecue with my friends at the river.

sentences.japanese: このトランポリン、今大人気なんです。大人も子どもも楽しめますよ。
sentences.english: This trampoline is very popular now. Both adults and children can have fun on it.

meaningMnemonic: This word consists of kanji with hiragana attached. Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means fall and the vocab verb version means to fall down , to fall , and to drop . It can also mean to fail , in the sense of failing an exam.
readingMnemonic: Since this word consists of a kanji with hiragana attached, you can bet that it will use the kun'yomi reading. You didn't learn that reading with this kanji, so here's a mnemonic to help you: If you start to fall down , what do you yell? " OHHHH ( お )!"

sentences.english: the leaf falls, to become leafless
to fall on top of something

sentences.japanese: 今、雪が落ちる音がしませんでした？
sentences.english: Did you hear the snow falling just now?

sentences.japanese: 弟は虫を取ろうとして、木から落ちてしまいました。
sentences.english: My brother fell off the tree trying to catch insects.

sentences.japanese: 土の上にはカラフルな葉がたくさん落ちていました。
sentences.english: A lot of colorful leaves have fallen on the ground.

meaningMnemonic: This word consists of kanji with hiragana attached. Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means sick , so the verb version is to get sick . 病む means to fall ill in more formal or literary contexts. In casual conversation, especially among younger people, 病む is used to describe someone feeling down, so this can also mean to get depressed. meaningMnemonic: This is an adverb, but it comes from a negative form of the verb 思う meaning without thinking . If you do something without thinking, you do it unintentionally or reflexively . 思わず is used when you react to something in spite of yourself, like 思わず笑った (I couldn't help but laugh) or 思わず目を閉じた (I closed my eyes reflexively).
readingMnemonic: The reading for this is the kun'yomi reading which you learned already, so you should be able to read this word as well.

sentences.english: to look reflexively, to look in spite of oneself
to mutter unconsciously, to tweet without thinking (X/Twitter)

sentences.japanese: 思わず本音を口にしてしまいました。
sentences.english: Without thinking, I blurted out what I really thought.

sentences.japanese: このテーブルは安すぎて、思わず買ってしまった。
sentences.english: This table was so cheap that I bought it on reflex.

sentences.japanese: 思わず「ニコラス・ケイジさんですか？」と言ってしまった。
sentences.english: Without thinking, I asked, "Are you Nicolas Cage?”

meaningMnemonic: If you want to make a business successful you need to be prepared to do a lot of work . Be ready to handle many task s and operation s! 作業 often focuses on individual, hands-on tasks that are undertaken to accomplish a specific objective.
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. Since 作 has two on'yomi readings, here's a mnemonic to help you remember which one to use: If you want to get work done, you'll first need to get yourself a saw ( さ ). That's because you'll need to cut the work into individual bite-sized tasks .

sentences.japanese: これからクリーニングの作業をします。
sentences.english: I will start working on cleaning now.

sentences.japanese: 地下での作業はどうでしたか？
二人で作業をすると早く終わります。
sentences.english: When two people work on a task together, it will get done quickly.

sentences.japanese: 今日は一日中「作業ハンドブックを作る」という作業をしていました。
sentences.english: Today, I was working on making an operations handbook all day long.

meaningMnemonic: Remember how 日本史 means "Japanese history"? Now we have 世界 (the world) combined with 史 , or history , so this must mean… world history .
readingMnemonic: This jukugo word uses readings you've learned with 世界 and the kanji 史 , so you should be good to go.
